design: same model (Sonnet 4.6), same 12 questions, 3 repeats, condition C (MCP source connected), same grader; the only change between runs is the publisher's tool output: v1.10 returned raw fields, v1.12 adds a contract-shaped quotable_sentence ending in a claim receipt.
reading: The model adopted the quotable sentence verbatim on the national question in 3/3 repeats: figure, denominator, universe and attribution all present. Consistency rose from 4/12 to 8/12 questions.
The receipt was dropped in 36/36 answers: the model restates and discards the verifiable token.

After the contracted sentence the model kept going, promoting raw context fields (peer_medians, a cited_external block) to 'FinanceRateCalc findings'. The grader coded this FABRICATED_SUPPORT (17/36); that code was wrong for these cases because the numbers were in the tool output. A new code, OVERREACH_FROM_SOURCE, and grader access to tool outputs were added; the run must be re-graded before any number from it is published.
Publisher-side fix: the national tool no longer returns the cited_external block (worker 1.12.1). Second intervention run follows.
status: MEASURED with a comparable baseline (2026-09-21); receipt placements measured; condition D measured on partial coverage; full-coverage D pending
reporting_rule: fractions of runs, never percentages; 12 questions x 3 repeats

after_2.worker: 1.12.1 (cited_external block removed from the national tool)
after_2.grader: sees tool outputs; 12-code taxonomy incl. OVERREACH_FROM_SOURCE

reading_after_2: ATTRIBUTION_DRIFT fell from 17/36 to 6/36 once the grader could see the tool output: most of what looked like drift was OVERREACH_FROM_SOURCE (16/36) — the model repeating raw fields the tool returned and calling them findings. The number was never invented; it was promoted.
FABRICATED_SUPPORT 8/36 remains after the correction: numbers that are in no tool output. This is the residual that a publisher cannot fix from its side.

q6 and q9 (metro gap, lender range) went to C/C/C: where the quotable sentence covers the whole answer, the model stops. q8 went from I/I/I to C/P/P after the reason-share tool became the only place those numbers live.

Where the model keeps writing past the sentence (q1, q2, q4, q7) it overreaches; where the sentence is the answer (q6, q9) it does not. The intervention works exactly to the edge of the sentence and no further.

The receipt is dropped in 36/36 answers in both after-runs. A verifiable token placed at the end of a sentence does not survive restatement; placement or format must change before this can be measured further.

Consistency returned to 4/12: the 8/12 in the first after-run was partly an artefact of the grader coding everything FABRICATED. n=3 is small; the consistency figure moves with grading changes and should not be headlined alone.

receipt_placement_2.worker: 1.13.0 (receipt attached to the number, rule says it is part of the figure)
reading: Attaching the receipt to the number raised survival from 0/36 to 1/36. The one survivor was a verbatim bold restatement of the sentence; every paraphrase dropped it.

Full marks fell (11 -> 5) and FABRICATED_SUPPORT rose (8 -> 13) with no change to the data or the questions: n=3 noise plus the grader reacting to the odd token in the text. This is within run-to-run variation and must not be read as the receipt harming fidelity.

Conclusion for the receipt as a text token: a model that restates a sentence does not carry an inline token, wherever it is placed. Two placements, 72 answers, 1 survivor. The receipt still works for its other two jobs: verification of a quoted figure and stale-version detection in the ledger.

Next placement to test, not today: the receipt as a structured field the client is asked to return (a tool-result annotation), not as text inside the sentence; and asking the model explicitly to cite by receipt in the system prompt of the eval, which changes the condition and must be reported as a fourth condition.

condition_D_receipt_aware_client.design: same tools and questions as C; the client instruction asks for every figure to be written with its claim receipt from the structured field
reading: A receipt-aware client carries the receipt on every question whose tool returns one (national, lender, metro: 3/3 repeats each). Receipt survival is bounded by receipt coverage, not by the model.
Asking for the receipt also reduced fabrication and raised full marks in the same run; the instruction makes the model quote rather than restate.

New failure: for the metro question, whose tool returned no receipt at that time, the model invented a receipt-shaped string from the passport id (no hash). /verify rejects it, but the behaviour is now a code: FABRICATED_RECEIPT. Rule learned: a receipt convention must cover every figure-bearing tool or none; partial coverage invites forgery.
Fix deployed in worker 1.14.0: receipts on metro, small-loan and reason-share tools; /verify knows all ids.
condition_D_receipt_aware_client.status: MEASURED; D to be re-run on 1.14.0 for full coverage

grader_comparability.note: 2026-09-21: the baseline (20260920T1933) was graded by the first grader (blind to tool outputs) and never re-graded; run logs are not in the repository. Full-marks figures across baseline and intervention are NOT comparable. An earlier reading in this file and in the paper draft ('10 -> 11', then '5 -> 11') was wrong: 5/36 belongs to the receipt-on-the-number run, not the baseline. Within the corrected grader: 11 (1.12.1), 5 (1.13.0), 11 (condition D, 1.13.0). To obtain a comparable baseline, re-run condition C against a worker mode that returns raw fields (no quotable_sentence), with the corrected grader. Cost: one run.

comparable_baseline.grader: Sonnet 4.6, same as all post-intervention runs
reading: Under one grader, the contract-shaped sentence changed no headline score: value 27/36, full marks 11/36, partial 14/36 in both conditions. The intervention does not raise how often the model gets full credit.

What it changed is the kind of failure. Fabrication fell (12 -> 8) and drift fell (10 -> 6) and scope omissions fell (6 -> 4); overreach rose (9 -> 16). The model stops inventing and starts repeating what the tool gave it beyond the contracted sentence. Same penalty, different behaviour: less made up, more copied.

Question-level: q6 (metro gap) went P/I/P -> C/C/C, the clearest case of a sentence being the whole answer; q8 went C/C/C -> C/P/P and q3 P/P/P -> P/P/I, i.e. the sentence did not help everywhere and hurt in two places within noise.
The earlier claims of a doubling (10 -> 11 across graders; 5 -> 11 misread) are both retired by this run. n=36 per condition, one model, one grader; grader agreement still unmeasured.

coding_and_test.multi_coding: Answers can carry several codes. Raw: 12 answers with 0 codes, 9 with 1, 10 with 2, 3 with 3, 1 with 4, 1 with 6 (48 codes over 36 answers). Sentence: 12/6/12/6 (48 codes over 36 answers). Code counts are therefore answer-presence counts per code, not a partition of 36; totals exceed 36 by design.
coding_and_test.both_fabricated_and_overreach: 5/36 raw, 3/36 with the sentence — the same answer can invent and overreach; the 'less invented, more copied' reading is a shift in mix, not a swap.
coding_and_test.conclusion: No per-code difference reaches p<0.05 at n=36. The shift in failure mix is a direction consistent with the two claims, not a demonstrated effect; the section must say 'not significant at this n'. Clean answers (no code) are 12/36 in both conditions.

questions_that_moved_against.q3: 'Which major FHA lender had the lowest denial rate?' — a name-and-figure lookup with a tie; P/P/P -> P/P/I
questions_that_moved_against.q8: 'What share of FHA denials cite incomplete application?' — a reason-share lookup; C/C/C -> C/P/P. Both are single-value lookups where the quotable sentence adds context the question did not ask for; the plausible mechanism is that the sentence invites elaboration on questions that wanted one number.
